sector_model: Industrial manufacturer with percent-of-completion revenue: P/E, FCF after capex build, working capital, restatement risk.
thesis: AAON (Nasdaq: AAON): HVAC rooftop units, coils and data center cooling (BASX). Q3 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-11-09) read. Q3 sales 707.4M (+84.1%), 9M 1,842.1M (+81.0%); BASX +207% and Coil Products +174% in Q3 on a large liquid cooling order; consolidated gross margin 26.7% vs 27.8%, AAON Oklahoma margin 25.5% vs 33.0% on Memphis plant overhead. 9M NI 172.5M vs 75.6M. 9M OCF 146.9M, capex 138.1M (9M FCF 8.8M); receivables +26% and inventories +44% since year end. On 2026-11-09 the 8-K Item 4.02 says Q1 and Q2 2026 10-Qs should not be relied on (percent-of-completion revenue and software subscription errors; restated Q1 NI 36.5M vs 39.8M, six-month NI 103.6M vs 96.5M) and the 10-Q reports a material weakness in BASX revenue controls. Close 75.21 (2026-11-20) x 82.46M = 6.20B = 30.3x TTM NI 204.6M; TTM FCF not computed (FY25 capex missing).
counterthesis: A restatement and an open material weakness in the segment driving most growth means the revenue base is the key risk; percent-of-completion revenue on large data center orders is judgment-heavy; cash conversion is poor (9M FCF 8.8M on NI 172.5M, working capital build); gross margin fell; customer concentration in a few large orders not checked; new 250M term loan adds debt; at 30x earnings the stock prices continued hypergrowth.
invalidation: Do not upgrade until the material weakness is remediated and a clean audited 10-K is filed; downgrade to avoid if further restatement, order cancellations, or negative operating cash flow recur.
